subject: social_science
chapter_title: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments

concepts.title: Government and the Ruler's Duties
concepts.definition: Government is the machinery that rules a country on the people's behalf; Kautilya sums a ruler's internal duties as three-fold, raksha or protection from aggression, palana or law and order within, and yogakshema or the welfare of the people.
concepts.key_idea: Whoever rules is answerable for safety, order and welfare; types of government differ in who checks that answer.

concepts.title: Democracy: Direct and Representative
concepts.definition: In a democracy the people are the source of power: direct democracy lets all citizens decide together, while representative democracy, India's model, elects law-makers who answer to voters at fixed intervals.
concepts.key_idea: Democracy turns rulers into servants: power is lent by the people and recalled at the ballot box.

concepts.title: Monarchy and Other Forms of Rule
concepts.definition: In a monarchy rule passes by birth within a royal family, and the ruler is not elected; the chapter studies a different kind of monarchy too, where the king's power is checked by custom and counsel.
concepts.key_idea: Monarchy bets on birth, democracy on ballots; history shows both can rule well or badly, but only one answers to the people.

concepts.title: Who Checks the Rulers
concepts.definition: Every form of government needs a check: democracies use constitutions and elections, even monarchies leaned on dharma and counsellors; where no check exists, the ruled have no remedy against misrule.
concepts.key_idea: Power without accountability decays: the health of any government lies in what can question it.
